ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows part of a TTL gate, with a +5 V power supply marked at the top. On the left there is a 4 kΩ resistor, and in the middle upper part there is a 1.4 kΩ resistor. On the far right is the output-stage transistor, whose emitter is grounded, whose collector is connected to the output terminal Vo, and marked with sinking current I. The base of this right-side transistor is driven by the middle node; this base-driving node is also connected to the upper end of a 1 kΩ resistor, the lower end of the 1 kΩ resistor is grounded, and the IR asked for in the problem is the current of this resistor. Reasoning: When the output is logic 0, the far-right grounded-emitter output transistor is on and is in the saturated state. The problem gives the VBE of the saturated transistor as 0.75 V, therefore the base node voltage of the right-side transistor is 0.75 V. This node is also the voltage at the upper end of the 1 kΩ resistor, and the lower end is grounded, so IR = 0.75 V / 1 kΩ = 0.00075 A = 0.75 mA.

method.method_draft: First describe the circuit: identify the rightmost grounded-emitter output transistor and the 1 kΩ resistor connected from its base-drive node to ground. Because the output is at logic 0, take the rightmost transistor as saturated. Its base-emitter voltage is therefore 0.75 V, so the node at the top of the 1 kΩ resistor is 0.75 V above ground. The current through that resistor is IR = 0.75/1000 A = 0.75 mA.
